newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's APV to maintain Co-Nexus contract.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's APV to maintain Co-Nexus contract.

text.p: Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt decided to maintain its asset handling contract with Co-Nexus Vagyonkezelo Holding Kft until it runs out at the end of this year, APV officials said on Thursday.
"We had the choice of a bad or a worse decision," APV president Arpad Kovacs told a news conference.

Hungary's Securities and Bourse Supervision (AETF) last month suspended the activities of Co-Nexus's brokerage until January 31 and appointed a commissioner to supervise the company after a collapse in investor confidence in the company on doubts whether it could repay its debts to APV.

Co-Nexus was commissioned in 1992 by APV's predecessor, the State Property Agency (AVU), to manage state-owned property worth a nominal four billion forints over a four-year period, ending on December 31.

Earlier press reports suggested the property might have been overvalued and said it was unlikely the company could pay back the amount at the expiry of its contract. Other reports raised doubts about the portfolio's management.
AVU was dissolved by the present government last year and replaced by APV Rt, which also incorporated the old State Asset Handling Agency.
APV said the AVU contract was inadequate in that it gave Co-Nexus free rein over the portfolio and no rights of intermediate control to APV.
"According to the contract, anything could be done with the assets," APV's general director Pal Szabo said.
Szabo declined to comment on the size of expected losses but added that breaching the contract at this late stage would have only caused "an infinite number of accounting problems".
